intro.text: Halcyon FM. 98.6 on the dial. 3:40 in the morning.
98.6. Body temperature. Somebody in marketing had a sense of humour. Or didn't, which is funnier.
Detective {name}! Welcome back, {sir}. Not that you were anywhere. That anyone's told me about.
Good recovery, Pike. What do we have?
Desmond Calloway. 'Dez.' Hosts The Small Hours, midnight to four. It's a call-in show. Lonely people, mostly.
His producer found him at ten past three. Coroner's been and gone. Says he died between one and two.

intro_narrow.text: I asked. He said he could, but then he'd only be wrong more precisely.

intro_rest.text: Here's the thing, {sir}. The show ran until 2:40. Callers and everything. I had it on in the car.
So either the coroner's wrong, or you spent an hour being kept company by a dead man.
I did think he sounded tired.
Tap things to examine them. Swipe sideways to turn and face another wall. 'Look around' shows what's worth a tap.

body.text: He isn't going to add anything. First time in thirty years.
Desmond Calloway. One blow, back of the head. He was facing the glass and he stayed facing it.
No defensive wounds, {sir}. The book says that means he trusted his killer.
Or he was mid-sentence. Radio people can't hear a thing while they're talking. I think that's the appeal.
Still. You don't turn your back on a stranger. You turn it on somebody who's walked in a thousand times.

mic.text: Still live, technically. Fifty thousand watts of a man not saying anything.
Leave it. It's the most honest hour this station's ever broadcast.

mug.text: Halcyon FM mug. Coffee, by the colour. Bourbon, by everything else.

mug_down.text: Three years, two months. I put it down.

do: remember You took a long second look at a dead man's bourbon.
mug_linger.text: Three years, two months. It still smells like a good idea.

phone.text: Line three's dark now. First time tonight anyone at this station has hung up properly.
Line three is blinking. Someone's on hold.
The little counter says an hour and fifty minutes. That isn't a caller, Pike. That's a hostage.

choice.text: This is Detective {name}, city police. Who am I speaking to?
Dez can't come to the phone.

iris_cant.text: He was an optimist. This is Detective {name}. And you are?

iris_story.text: Iris. He calls me the Night Owl. I ring most nights. I've been holding since 1:26. I wrote it down. I write everything down; it's cheaper than being listened to.
You've been on hold for nearly two hours.
I've held longer for the gas company, and they have never once asked after my sister.
What did he say before he put you on hold?
He said, 'Hang on, Owl. The Boss just walked in.' Then the hold music. It's his own theme tune. You'd think that would have warned me about him years ago.
And then at a quarter past two I'm sat here, on hold, and I hear myself on the radio. Telling the one about my sister's wedding.
I told that story in March. I was funnier in March.

choice.text: Thank you, Iris. You've helped more than you know.
Stay by your phone. An officer will take a statement.
You can hang up now, ma'am.

do: remember You told the Night Owl the truth, and took your time over it.
iris_kind.text: ...I'll leave the radio on anyway. For the hum.

iris_book.text: I'm always by my phone, Detective. That's the whole trouble.

clipboard.text: Blank after 1:04. Tidy handwriting, right up until there isn't any.
Call sheet. The producer screens each caller and writes them up for the host. 'Walter, line two, his ex-wife's new boat.'
Last entry, 1:04. After that, nothing. Either the city ran out of lonely people at four minutes past one, or somebody put the pencil down.

bin.text: Takeout menus and a parking ticket from 1987. He was contesting it on principle.
Wastebasket. Takeout menus, a parking ticket, and one sheet of station letterhead balled up tight. Somebody threw that with feeling.

bin_letter.text: 'Gordon - effective Friday, I'm done. Coastal have offered me syndication and a chair that reclines. Typed 12:40 a.m., between the weather and the lonely. - D.'
Across it, in red pen and a different hand: 'Over my dead body. - G.'
He typed the time on his own resignation letter?
Radio man. They log everything. It's how they know they were there.

trophy.text: Voice of the City, 1989. It got the last word after all.
Golden Microphone, 1989. 'Voice of the City.' Brass on a marble base. The shelf has a year of dust on it, and this is sitting in a clean square slightly too big for it.
Picked up, put back, and wiped. It's the shiniest thing in the building, careers included.

trophy_base.text: They wiped the brass and forgot the engraving. There's blood in the second nine of 1989.
The murder weapon was his own award?
It was within reach. Nobody walks in planning to kill a man with his own shelf.

on_air.text: ON AIR. Still lit. Nobody's told the sign.

clock.text: Runs four minutes fast. In radio that isn't a fault, it's a policy.

poster.text: 'Dez Calloway - The Small Hours.' The publicity photo. Fifteen years and one hairline ago.
He's pointing at the camera. They always point. As though you were the one who'd rung in.

reel.text: Seventy minutes of a man's better nights, going round and round with nothing left on it.
The emergency reel. Run right out, and still turning.

reel_first.text: Reel-to-reel deck. The take-up reel's full and the tail of the tape is slapping round and round. Nobody stopped it. It just ran out.
Label on the box: 'IN CASE OF DEZ - 70 min. - M.Q.'
In case of Dez, Pike. I'm told it's a complete sentence once you've met him.

choice.text: [Look at how the tape is threaded.]

reel_threading.text: The tape skips the tension arm altogether. Straight off the reel and across the heads. It'll play like that. It'll also spill at the end, which it did.
It works the way a necktie works as a belt. Whoever did this had seen it done. They'd never done it.

cabinet.text: One empty slot, marked EMERGENCY. Somebody agreed that it was.
Tape cabinet. Steel, with a proper lock, standing open. One empty slot, and a label under it: EMERGENCY.
No scratches on the lock, {sir}. I checked twice. The second time was for fun.
So it was opened with a key, by someone who didn't think to lock up afterwards. People in a hurry are tidy about the wrong things.
